testRule: The first five topic videos are implementation tests, not proof of audience performance. Do not turn offline QA into a retention claim until videos are published and platform data is available.

videos.learning: The product-specific opening can stay in plain English while still teaching three different image jobs; the final sync pass reduced the largest voice gap to 5.59 seconds.
The same scorecard works when the proof changes from appearance to controls and use; the category-specific button check is clearer than generic image advice.
The category's real buyer question—fit, sole, heel, and true color—can be stated without technical photography language.
Scale, strap, opening, and inside space are stronger story beats than generic luxury language.
A concrete visual risk—glare hiding the hands, numbers, or crown—is more useful than saying the image should feel premium.

repeatedImplementationFindings: The actual recorder timeline must be the source of truth; sourceStartMs prevents voice lines from drifting from UI action.
Wait narration must be generated from each run's real generation_started-to-generation_ready duration; fixed wait tips created a 70-second silent hole in ECO08.
The sync QA gate now fails a kit when any spoken-audio gap exceeds 10 seconds; the repaired first five pass with maximum gaps from 3.96 to 6.29 seconds.
The horizontal renderer can use safe center keyframes and modest zoom without cutting the central action.
The top-right Airveek logo is readable without covering the app's own top-left logo.
Segment count should follow the real generation wait rather than a fixed 21-segment template; short waits stay short and long waits receive useful, category-specific checks.
The failed first ECO01 attempt showed that generation and browser-video finalization need separate QA checks.
publishingMetricsToAdd: whether viewers ask for the next product category
